- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% above recent mean), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast at +5% above recent high.
- If sentiment is positive but price is trending down, model often ignores trend reversal — adjust downward by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in volatile periods — if 3–5 consecutive days show strong downward momentum, add 1–3% downward bias to next forecast.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to overfit recent noise — smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values unless sentiment strongly signals direction.
- If forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., >10% over 3–5 days), reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence with true trend.
- If sentiment shows strong negative momentum (e.g., 3 consecutive negative values), model often fails to recognize risk — add 2–5% downward buffer to forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates short-term volatility — reduce forecast variance by 15–20% if sentiment is uncertain or mixed.
